LED substitution, boiler and hydronic distribution system improvements, and the installation and explanation of programmable thermostats each contributed to the overall reduction in energy use. Over the monitoring period, electricity consumption declined from 28,600 kWh to 16,800 kWh, while fuel oil consumption dropped from 3,220 gallons to 1,641 gallons. These reductions translate into meaningful financial benefits, though the precise dollar value is difficult to calculate. Reported ECIs have been adjusted to 2024-dollar values to account for inflation (Figure 5); however, such adjustments remain imperfect because of the complex financial landscape and the eight-year gap between the baseline (2016) and follow-up (2024) periods. In islanded locations like Aniak, bulk fuel oil purchases are transported by seasonal barge, delaying local cost adjustments relative to national price indices. EUI may serve as a more reliable reference point for assessing performance improvements over such a relatively short monitoring period. Given the outcomes of the Tribal Office retrofit, NVA could seek additional funding sources. Extending the scope of these energy efficiency improvements to essential community facilities, such as the Community Center, Duplex, and AVCP Office—initially identified in the original audits—could further amplify community-wide benefits. Implementing similar retrofit strategies across these additional buildings could yield further reductions in energy use and operational costs, without necessitating significant alterations to the building's construction. Weather events and shifting flight schedules can cause delays at any time of year. All supplies must be externally sourced, either shipped ahead of time by barge or delivered by plane, and all hazardous waste must be removed at additional cost. Price increases and supply chain demands caused by the global effects of the COVID-19 pandemic were significant barriers to this project and exacerbated existing logistics difficulties for a construction project in rural Alaska.
